T2_privileged_frame.name: ether_at_rest_earth_moves
T2_privileged_frame.statement: The ether is at rest and the earth is moving through it.

T2_privileged_frame.name: light_velocity_in_stationary_ether
T2_privileged_frame.statement: V is the velocity of light in the ether supposed stationary.

T2_privileged_frame.name: apparatus_moves_through_resting_ether
T2_privileged_frame.statement: When the ether is at rest and the whole apparatus moves in the direction sc with the velocity of the earth, the directions and distances traversed by the rays are altered.

T2_privileged_frame.name: bodies_have_motion_relative_to_ether
T2_privileged_frame.statement: Material bodies have a motion relative to the ether.

T2_privileged_frame.name: secular_experiments_can_observe_variation
T2_privileged_frame.statement: Secular experiments on electrical attractions between permanently electrified bodies can observe a variation of attraction due to motion relative to the ether.

T2_privileged_frame.name: quiescent_aether_is_newtonian_rest
T2_privileged_frame.statement: The spacial framework in absolute rest introduced by Newton is in fact the quiescent underlying æther.

T2_privileged_frame.name: earth_rotation_shifts_bands
T2_privileged_frame.statement: The earth's rotation through a stationary ether would produce a shift of the bands proportional to the area of the interference square.

T2_privileged_frame.name: turntable_rotation_shifts_bands
T2_privileged_frame.statement: Rotating the whole apparatus, telescope, and observer on a turntable through a stationary ether would produce a reversible shift of the bands.

T2_privileged_frame.name: stellar_aberration_favours_stationary

T3_local_time_artifice.name: auxiliary_time_variable_device
T3_local_time_artifice.statement: A change of the time-variable makes the equations revert to the same type as those referred to axes at rest, apart from the factor ε.

T3_local_time_artifice.name: true_time_defines_corresponding_instants
T3_local_time_artifice.statement: Corresponding instants at two points are defined by equating the true time at one point to the local time at the other.

T1_hits.statement: Absolute time, of itself and from its own nature, flows equably without regard to anything external.

T1_hits.statement: There may be no equable motion in nature, yet the progress of absolute time is liable to no change.
